name: עַמִּיהוּד
summary: Borne by the Ephraimite, son of Laadan, whose son Elishama was prince of Ephraim and led its host when Israel set out from Sinai (Num 1:10; 2:18; 7:48, 53; 10:22; 1Ch 7:26); by the fathers of Shemuel of Simeon and Pedahel of Naphtali, who were to divide the land (Num 34:20, 28); by the father of Talmai, king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled (2Sa 13:37, written עמיחור, read עַמִּיהוּד); and by a man of Judah after the return (1Ch 9:4). It is עַם “people, kinsman” with the ־ִי of “my”, and הוֹד “majesty”: “my kinsman is majesty”, the kinsman being God, whose garment is הוֹד (Psa 104:1), as in the names עַמִּיאֵל and אֱלִיאָב.

evidence.note: The standard of the camp of the sons of Ephraim set out, and over its host אֱלִישָׁמָע בֶּן־עַמִּיהוּד.
For Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, among the men who stood with Moses and Aaron to number Israel.
The line of Ephraim: Laadan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son.
For Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud, to divide the land.
For Naphtali, Pedahel son of Ammihud.
Absalom fled to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur; the written text has עמיחור.
Uthai son of Ammihud, of the sons of Perez son of Judah, dwelling in Jerusalem.
Yahweh is clothed with הוֹד וְהָדָר: the majesty the name speaks of.
Abraham “was gathered to his עַמִּים”: עַם as one’s kin.
A priest shall not defile himself for the dead “among his עַמִּים”, his kin.

note: BDB files the name apart (p.dj.aj, with no root); it is linked to the hod entry for its second element. p.dj.al is BDB’s cross-reference for the Kethiv עמיחור of 2Sa 13:37 and has no tokens of its own. The ־ִי may be “my” or a joining vowel (“kinsman of majesty”, “people of majesty”). TIPNR’s Ammihud@Num.1.10 is the Ephraimite of Num 10:22 and 1Ch 7:26. The names אֲבִיהוּד “my father is majesty” and אֲחִיהוּד “my brother is majesty” are formed the same way but have no name entries yet.
